title: Capture-head rewind of the threaded map
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For any valid input-head position $p$ and any natural number $j$ no greater than the length of the output in $c$, running the threaded-map controller for $j+1$ steps from the configuration that preserves $c$'s tape bank, has the controller in its capture-rewind state, places the input head at $p$ and the capture head at displacement $j-1$, and has empty output, yields the configuration with the controller in its input-rewind state, input head still at $p$, capture head at displacement $0$, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
c is a configuration of M on x
p is a valid input-head position
j is a natural number with j no greater than the length of c's output
replaced:
From the controller's capture-rewind state with the capture head at
displacement $j-1$, for any $j$ at most the captured word's length, exactly
$j+1$ silent steps return the capture head to displacement $0$ and enter the
input-rewind phase, with the input position unchanged.
